### 1 — Scene
An Asian-style meal: shredded vegetable salad with browned protein strips, plus fresh rice-paper rolls and sushi. I’m counting **both main plates on the tray**, excluding the fruit bowl at the left edge, drinks, and condiment cups.

### 2 — Vessels
Both main plates appear approximately **26 cm in diameter**. Each plate’s area is:
**3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm²**.

### 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
The salad’s browned strips appear to be tofu, though chicken is also possible. The dressing estimate reflects the visible light coating.

| Visible item | Plate area covered | Area × average height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shredded cabbage, carrot, and greens | 42% of salad plate | 223 × 1.8 = 401 ml | 0.50 | 201 g | 25 | 50 kcal |
| Browned tofu strips | 18% | 96 × 0.7 = 67 ml | 0.95 | 64 g | 160 | 102 kcal |
| Light oily dressing | 5% equivalent area | 27 × 0.3 = 8 ml | 1.00 | 8 g | 500 | 40 kcal |
| Two fresh rice-paper rolls | 30% of roll plate | 159 × 1.6 = 254 ml | 0.90 | 229 g | 150 | 344 kcal |
| Assorted vegetable sushi pieces | 24% | 127 × 1.8 = 229 ml | 0.80 | 183 g | 145 | 265 kcal |

### 8 — Sanity check
The allocated coverage totals **65% of the salad plate** and **54% of the roll plate**, leaving substantial exposed rims. Approximately **685 g and 800 kcal across two plates** is plausible for the visible quantity. Roll fillings and the protein’s identity are the largest uncertainties.
